approved: Independent Parliamentary Expenses Authority (Consequential Amendments) Bill 2017

The speaker argued that the bills to establish the Independent Parliamentary Expenses Authority (IPEA) will improve transparency and public trust, while noting that 87% of current MPs—those elected after 2004—no longer receive a pension or generous travel allowances. He welcomed the authority for clarifying expense rules and providing a reference point for MPs, though he cautioned that oversight costs may exceed savings.

The Independent Parliamentary Expenses Authority (Consequential Amendments) Bill 2017 is the first step in the biggest reforms to managing parliamentarians' expenses in more than a generation, establishing a new authority to provide clear guidance and ensure accountability. The government will continue implementing recommendations from an independent entitlements review, and a consequential amendment to the Freedom of Information Act will allow the authority to give confidential advice on travel expenses.
